title: How many sixth pieces fill the length of one third?
description: On the fraction wall, sixth pieces are laid end to end along the row of thirds. Six sixth pieces fill the whole and one third is one of three equal parts, so the pieces are shared out in threes. Keeko doubts it by reading the number three in one third as the count.
teaching_notes: One idea: six sixth pieces make one whole, and one third is one of three equal parts of it. Watch for students who read the denominator as the number of pieces that fill the length.

source: Using a fraction wall with rows of thirds and sixths, how ma
video_script.why: The child counts how many pieces of one sixth fill one third by splitting the six pieces of the whole into three equal parts.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own fraction wall with rows of thirds and sixths
video_script.anchor: the fraction wall of the book: one whole and rows of equal pieces
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says three pieces, because one third has a three in it. Three sixth pieces laid on the third piece run past its end; the three in one third tells how many thirds fill the whole, not how many sixths.
video_script.payoff_line: Two pieces of one sixth make the length of one third
video_script.fraction_reading: one third, one sixth, two sixths, six sixths
maths_rules: fraction wall rows of thirds and sixths
1/3 is one of 3 equal parts of the whole, so it needs one third of the 6 pieces
6 divided by 3 = 2, so 2 pieces of 1/6 make 1/3 (2/6 = 1/3)
slip: Keeko thinks 3 pieces because 1/3 has a 3 in it; 3 pieces of 1/6 are 3/6 = 1/2, which is more than 1/3
video_script.design: One idea: count the sixth pieces that make the whole, then share them into three equal parts. The sixth pieces are laid end to end under the row of thirds.
